title: Using the root's inorder position to split left and right subtrees, then splitting preorder
summary: The first preorder element, 3, identifies the root; inorder splits into left subtree [9] and right subtree [1,2,7], and those subtree sizes then split preorder.
context: The input is preorder traversal preorder = [3, 9, 2, 1, 7] and inorder traversal inorder = [9, 3, 1, 2, 7], with all node values distinct.
description: Preorder visits the root first, so the first element of preorder, 3, is the root.
Locate 3 in inorder: to its left is only [9] and to its right is [1,2,7], telling us that the left and right subtrees contain 1 node and 3 nodes, respectively.

Split preorder accordingly: the single element [9] right after root 3 belongs to the left subtree, and the remaining [2,1,7] belongs to the right subtree. Both traversals of the right subtree contain the same set of nodes, visited in different orders.

On the left side of the figure, the entire five-node tree is also drawn for reference. Below, the first table lists the traversal slices produced by this split, and the second table lists all parent-child links in the tree.
